newsitem.title: SENEGAL: Senegal to liberalise cellphone network next year.
newsitem.headline: Senegal to liberalise cellphone network next year.

text.p: Senegal, poised to privatise its telecommunication company SONATEL, said on Thursday that it would liberalise its cellular telephone sector next year -- with January as the target date for the start of a second network.
Communication Minister Serigne Diop told reporters the government would put the licence for a second operator out to international tender this year.
"From January 1998, we will have a second operator in the cellular phone service, for a start," he said.
SONATEL (Societe Nationale des Telecommunications du Senegal) started the West African nations' first cellular telephone service in October, using a GSM system.
Diop said the government was poised to finalise a provisional agreement with a Swedish-led consortium on the purchase of a strategic stake in SONATEL.
"We have almost finished. A final signing of the accord with the consortium will take place soon," he added.
Under the provisional deal, the consortium led by Telia Overseas of Sweden was to pay up to 70 billion CFA francs, representing one third of the projected capital of SONATEL.
Other members of the consortium include the Walter Group of the United States, China Telecommunication Services and private Senegalese company Senecom Partners.
The remaining shares were to be sold to private Senegalese and African investors with 10 percent allocated to SONATEL staff. It was not immediately clear how the shares would be marketed.
